_comment: The button-map token grammar, agreed between the admin API and the firmware.
The API validates a proposed map (Services/ButtonMap.cs) and the firmware parses
the one it is handed on the heartbeat (lib/court/ButtonMap.cpp). Neither can see
the other's source, and the failure they would produce is silent: a token one side
accepts and the other quietly ignores leaves a button that does nothing, or worse,
one that still does what it did before an admin changed it.
Both sides read this file. Drift turns a test red instead of turning a court off.
max_grant_minutes is pinned to relay_hard_cap_minutes on purpose (review M1). The relay
bank's own timer clamps actuation at relay_hard_cap_minutes whatever the grant says, so
a button that grants more sells minutes the lights cannot deliver: paid-for darkness
with no refund and no re-light path. Both sides refuse a grant past it.

actions.note: empty is none, so a blank field in an admin form is not an error
leading and trailing space tolerated; a hand-edited row has both

actions.why: courts are A-D and there is no fifth relay
a zero-minute grant is a button that lights a court and immediately releases it
one past the relay hard cap: the relay timer would cut the lights at 90 and the member paid for 91
the old cap (review M1): the LCD said 240 MIN, the lights died at minute 90, and the member's own booking blocked a re-purchase
no sign; a negative duration is a wrap on the device side
a trailing character must not be ignored — 6000x silently becoming 6000 is four days of lights

maps.name: default
maps.note: what the hand-built box already did; any other default would change every box's behaviour on first deploy

maps.name: swapped-courts
maps.note: the case the whole feature exists for: an admin reorders courts without touching a wire

maps.name: two-court-club
maps.note: unused buttons are legal, and the same action may appear twice

maps.name: no-court-button
maps.why: nothing can start a walk-up; almost certainly a half-finished edit

maps.name: too-few-entries
maps.why: eight buttons are soldered to the board; four entries leaves half the panel undefined
